text:
Maya (support): Hey team, just got a report from a customer (ACME) — they applied a promo code, received the free-trial credit in the UI, and their API requests return 200s, but their promo balance doesn't decrement. They sent logs showing successful responses and token counts. Can someone take a look? :thinking:

Anton (billing): Can you paste the request sample and the org/project IDs? Quick suspicion: promo grants are account-level but their requests might be going to a Dedicated project with separate billing mapping.

Maya (support): Good call. Their example request:```
curl -X POST https://dedicated-us.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-dedicated-xxxx" \
  -H "X-Project-ID: proj-acme-42" \
  -d '{"model":"rwkv-3b","input":"hello"}'
```They show token usage in response: "usage": {"input_tokens": 12, "output_tokens": 45} but ledger shows no debit and promo balance unchanged.

Jin (platform): Quick checks: is the API key the same org that received the promo? Dedicated endpoints sometimes route billing through the project billing_id. If the promo was issued to org:acct-acme but the dedicated project maps to billing_id:dedicated-acct, debits might bypass the promo bucket.

Maya (support): I confirmed the promo grant: promo_id=promo-2026-summer tied to org acct-acme. The API key on the request belongs to project proj-acme-42 (billing_id: dedicated-acme-7). So that matches the mismatch theory.

Anton (billing): That explains it. Promo grants are currently keyed to org-level ledgers in hosted mode. We didn't propagate promo entitlements to Dedicated project ledgers in the billing router. So Dedicated consumes but charges against project ledger without applying promo credits.

BillingBot: AUTO-ALERT: Created billing-issue/4289 for "Promo not applied to Dedicated project ledgers". Priority: P2. Assigned to Anton.

Anton (billing): I'll own the fix. Short-term mitigation: advise customer to either (A) call the hosted endpoint with their org-level API key (which will consume promo credits), or (B) I can transfer a promo credit balance into their dedicated project ledger manually. Which do they prefer?

Maya (support): I asked the customer; they prefer the manual transfer today and plan to stay on Dedicated long-term.

Anton (billing): Ok, I'll run a one-time transfer and then we need a code change: billing router should check for active promo entitlements at org level and apply to project-ledger debits when project is owned by that org. Patch plan: add promo lookup in router + unit tests. Will target next release.

Jin (platform): Once Anton has the transfer info, I can add instrumentation to the router to log when a promo entitlement is applied or skipped (log fields: org_id, project_id, promo_id, applied:true/false). That should make future debugging faster.

Maya (support): Customer confirmed manual transfer worked and their balance showed - they could see promo decrement after next request. Closing loop: Assigned billing-issue/4289 to Anton; platform improvement ticket PLAT-1121 for logging.

Anton (billing): Notes for the fix: edge cases — shared promos across child orgs, expired promos with reserved grants, and retroactive charges. I'll include a migration script to reconcile past Dedicated usage that didn't consume promo credits.

Maya (support): Thanks all. I'll follow up with the customer with the workaround and ETA for the fix. :thumbsup:
